detail.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Adds the `data` section to `PretrainConfigContainer`: `cfg.data.dataset` is **the** dataset config, Megatron Core's `GPTDatasetConfig` itself, built from the arguments, serialized into `run_config.yaml`, and handed to `BlendedMegatronDatasetBuilder` as is; `cfg.data.dataloader` holds the loader settings and `cfg.data.dataset_type` the dataset class the builder instantiates. The GPT dataset providers (`pretrain_gpt.py`, `pretrain_hybrid.py`, `pretrain_hybrid_flex.py`, `tools/prepare_cache.py`) build from it instead of re-reading the argparse namespace. In Megatron Core, the dataset configs move the assertions of their `__post_init__` to `validate()` (the checks that need no tokenizer in `validate_without_tokenizer()`, which `validate()` runs first and the container's `validate()` runs on its own) and have no `__post_init__` anymore, so the object can be constructed before its tokenizer exists (`BlendedMegatronDatasetBuilder` validates the config it is given); the derived values (`mock`, `split_matrix`, `token_dtype_code`) become read-only properties, and the FIM dataset moves from `megatron/training/datasets` to `megatron/core/datasets`. First PR of the DatasetConfig series (follow-ups: TokenizerConfig authoritative, dataloader and batch consumers, `seq_length` ownership).

## Issue tracking

Part of #3554 (args namespace to config container). Converges on the shape Megatron-Bridge uses for its dataset config.

## Design

- **One object, Core's.** `cfg.data.dataset` is `megatron.core.datasets.gpt_dataset.GPTDatasetConfig` (or its FIM subclass); there is no training-side subclass. Core's class no longer asserts in `__post_init__` what needs the tokenizer: those assertions are `validate()`, run once the config is complete (the tokenizer bound), and `validate()` asserts only. The derived values are read-only properties: `mock` and `split_matrix` of the sources and `split`, `token_dtype_code` of the bound tokenizer; nothing is derived into the object at any step. `BlendedMegatronDatasetConfig.validate_without_tokenizer()` holds the blend and split assertions, `validate()` runs it and then what needs the tokenizer, and nothing runs at construction (the base `__post_init__` is gone; the two Core subclasses that chained to it keep their own checks); `DataConfig.validate()` runs `validate_without_tokenizer()` (the GPT and FIM tokenizer-free checks included) for the container path, and `BlendedMegatronDatasetBuilder.__init__` calls `config.validate()`, so every caller that hands the builder a complete config is covered without an explicit call. `DataConfig.bind_tokenizer(tokenizer)` binds the run's tokenizer and runs Core's `validate()`; `initialize_runtime_services` does this right after the tokenizer is built, and `builder_inputs()` refuses an unbound config. The builder receives `cfg.data.dataset` itself: `builder.config is cfg.data.dataset`.
- **Fields other sections own.** Six Core fields are owned by other sections (the four parallel sizes by the model layout and the world size, the two validation flags by `validation`; `CONTAINER_WRITTEN_FIELDS`). The factory leaves them unset. `validate()` checks, with one explicit comparison per field, that a value given on the dataset config agrees with its owner, the way Megatron-Bridge checks `model.seq_length` against its dataset config; `finalize()` does the same for `data_parallel_size`, which needs the world size (`get_data_parallel_size(safe_get_world_size())` uses `GTPParallelLayout` with the configured context-parallel size, the quotient `validate_args` computes), then writes them, one assignment each (seven names since #7047: `dynamic_context_parallel` and its deprecated alias `hybrid_context_parallel`, which the container folds into the canonical field and clears). A layout field at Core's default (1, 0, False) carries no explicit value and is written over; without a model config (`pretrain_hybrid_flex.py`) the layout fields have no owner and keep what they hold; none of them is serialized with the section: what is saved reproduces the run. Standalone callers (`tools/prepare_cache.py`, the legacy `core_gpt_dataset_config_from_args` wrappers) fill them from `args`. `random_seed` is not a mirror: it is the data section's own setting, filled from `--seed` by the factory and saved with the section, independent of `rng.seed` after construction (Megatron-Bridge's semantics). Every command line behaves as on `main`; a `--dataset-seed` flag can follow when CLI control is wanted.
- **Only Core inputs on the object.** The data-path flags are resolved into `blend` / `blend_per_split` / `split` by the factory, `--per-dataset-sequences-path` is loaded into `sequences_per_dataset`, the five `--fim-*-token` flags fold into `fim_extra_tokens`. Megatron Core's `GPTFIMDatasetConfig` (the FIM dataset now lives in `megatron/core/datasets/gpt_fim_dataset.py`; `megatron.training.datasets.fim_dataset` re-exports both classes) carries the six FIM fields `GPTFIMDataset` reads and checks them in its own `validate()`. `--phase-transition-iterations` stays a training argument.
- **The dataset class is the selector.** `cfg.data.dataset_type` is the class (`GPTDataset`, `MockGPTDataset`, `GPTFIMDataset`, `SFTDataset`, `MockSFTDataset`, `VarlenDataset`, `MockVarlenDataset`), serialized as a `_target_` with `_call_: false`. On the CLI it follows the existing `--sft`, `--use-varlen-dataset`, `--mock-data` and `--fim-data` flags with the providers' precedence; no new flag. With no data source and no `--mock-data`, the mock class is selected where the entry point has one (with a warning), as Megatron-Bridge does. `resolve_dataset_class()` checks class and config agree (a mock class takes no source, a real class needs one, `GPTFIMDataset` goes with `GPTFIMDatasetConfig`).
- **One factory for the four entry points.** `gpt_data_config_from_args(args)` builds the same section for `pretrain_gpt.py`, `pretrain_hybrid.py`, `pretrain_hybrid_flex.py` and `tools/prepare_cache.py`; the differences between their legacy factories (fields never forwarded, requests silently downgraded to plain GPT) are not carried into the config. What a script cannot build it rejects itself: `pretrain_hybrid_flex.py` rejects `--use-varlen-dataset` (its batch path has no varlen support), the cache tool keeps rejecting `--mock-data`, `--sft` and `--fim-data` and pins the class to `GPTDataset`. No provider copies or edits the object.
- **Loader-only default.** Every other caller of `pretrain_cfg_container_from_args` (T5, BERT, VLM, the multimodal example, MiMo, RL, the ModelOpt fine-tuning example) gets `cfg.data` with the loader settings only (`dataset is None`): nothing dataset-related is validated, read or bound for them.
- **Providers unchanged in shape.** `training.py` is untouched: the GPT providers keep the legacy signature `(train_val_test_num_samples, vp_stage=None)` and the shared body reads `cfg.data` from the registered run config, as every provider reads `get_args()` today; `build_gpt_datasets` takes `data_config` explicitly for tests and direct callers.
- **One provider body.** `megatron/training/datasets/providers.py` holds `build_gpt_datasets` (the body of the GPT dataset provider: `cfg.data` in, `BlendedMegatronDatasetBuilder` fed with the config as is) and the GPT / hybrid rank predicate (`dataset_built_on_rank`, the rule from explicit inputs, and `is_dataset_built_on_rank`, the rule over the registered arguments, which it reads at call time from `megatron.training.global_vars` and `megatron.training.arguments`, where `tests/unit_tests/data/test_get_batch.py` patches them); `pretrain_gpt.py`, `pretrain_hybrid.py` and `pretrain_hybrid_flex.py` keep `train_valid_test_datasets_provider` as a wrapper of the legacy shape that calls it, hybrid-flex with its own predicate.

## Compatibility

- The parser is identical to `main`: no flag is added, moved or re-typed (snapshot test against the data arguments of `main`).
- `run_config.yaml` gains the `data` section; a file saved before it loads with the loader-only default.
- `core_gpt_dataset_config_from_args(args)`, the legacy call shape, is one helper in `argument_utils.py` (a standalone config built from the arguments, every data argument forwarded, the layout and validation fields and the seed from `args`, validated, bound to the tokenizer); `pretrain_gpt` and `pretrain_hybrid` re-export it and build their own tokenizer from `args` as before, `pretrain_hybrid_flex` wraps it with the global tokenizer as before, the cache tool wraps it with the class pinned to `GPTDataset`. The script-level names stay importable (`tests/unit_tests/distributed/mfsdp_v1` imports `pretrain_gpt.train_valid_test_datasets_provider`).
- `set_global_variables(args, cfg)` finalizes the container before the runtime services bind the tokenizer; since #8149 on `main` it finalizes every `PretrainConfigContainer`, and this PR changes nothing there anymore.
- Providers keep the positional contract `(train_val_test_num_samples, vp_stage=None)`; `training.py` is unchanged.
- Megatron Core: `GPTDatasetConfig(...)` constructs as before (same constructor fields and required arguments) and runs no check at construction anymore: the blend / split assertions and the tokenizer-dependent ones (the tokenizer, the `reset_*` / `eod_mask_loss` booleans, the SBHD / hybrid-CP exclusion, the `sequences_per_dataset` dtype requirement) are `validate()`'s, which `BlendedMegatronDatasetBuilder` runs (those that need no tokenizer are `validate_without_tokenizer()`'s, which `validate()` runs first); mock data uses the arbitrarily even split whatever `split` says, as before, with `split` left as given; the deprecated `hybrid_context_parallel` alias of #7047 is warned about and rejected next to `dynamic_context_parallel` by `validate_without_tokenizer()` but not rewritten there (`validate_args` and the training container normalize it; a Core-only caller sets `dynamic_context_parallel` itself); `MaskedWordPieceDatasetConfig` (BERT, T5) and `MultimodalDatasetConfig` keep their own `__post_init__` checks without chaining to a base method. `mock`, `split_matrix` and `token_dtype_code` are read-only properties instead of `init=False` fields: readers are unchanged, they cannot be assigned, `token_dtype_code` follows the tokenizer as soon as it is bound, and a mock config's `split` stays as given, `None` on the CLI without `--split` (the even split is `split_matrix`, whatever `split` says, as before); `sanitize_dataclass_config` drops the three names from older `run_config.yaml` files that carry them. A caller that wants the assertions before building calls `validate()`. `GPTFIMDatasetConfig.validate()` requires the two FIM rates and the five extra tokens to be given; a rate of `0.0` is a value, as before (`validate_args` keeps its own check for `--fim-data`).
- Megatron-Bridge: its `GPTDatasetConfig.finalize()` calls `super(MCoreGPTDatasetConfig, self).__post_init__()` explicitly (`training/config.py:332`), a method this PR removes, so Bridge's bump PR replaces that line with `super(MCoreGPTDatasetConfig, self).validate()` or `self.validate_without_tokenizer()` (the same checks); until then its data and training-config unit tests against this branch show 28 differing ids against `main` (210 failed on the branch, 182 on `main`), all failing inside `GPTDatasetConfig.finalize()` on the removed base `__post_init__`; with that one line applied to Bridge `d86a5c09b`, the same suites against this branch are identical to `main` again (0 differing ids of 1535). Agreed with the Megatron-Bridge PIC: Bridge adapts when it bumps its Megatron-LM pin. Everything else keeps working as is: its provider reads `mock` (a property), it binds the tokenizer in `setup()` before any build (so the builder's `validate()` passes, with the `reset_*` flags its `finalize()` asserts; its hand-written `token_dtype_code` assignment runs only when the value is `None`, which it no longer is once the tokenizer is bound), and its container calls `validate()` only on its SFT / HF / Energon configs. Two further bump items: the `token_dtype_code` block in `setup.py` is dead code, and the CLI translator's `dataset.mock=true` override for `--mock-data` names a read-only property. Bridge imports other sections of `megatron.training.config`, not the dataset one.

Documented behaviour differences, all intentional:

1. A request with no data source and no `--mock-data` selects the mock dataset class where the family has one (gpt, sft, varlen; fim has none and fails at validation), with a warning; the legacy providers keyed on `--mock-data` and paired a mock runtime config with the real dataset class, which failed to build.
2. `--mock-data` next to `--data-args-path` or `--per-split-data-args-path` (accepted by `validate_args`, which does not count file-backed sources) is rejected by the factory with the single-source message; the legacy providers paired `MockGPTDataset` with a config resolved from the file, which `MockGPTDataset` refuses, so the combination never trained.
3. `pretrain_hybrid.py` and `pretrain_hybrid_flex.py` build the requested dataset family, as `pretrain_gpt.py` does: `--fim-data` builds `GPTFIMDataset` where the legacy providers silently built plain GPT data, and `--sft --mock-data` builds `MockSFTDataset` where they selected the real `SFTDataset` around a mock config and failed inside the builder (`SFTLowLevelDataset(None)` raises `EmptyDatasetError`). On `pretrain_hybrid_flex.py` an SFT build, mock or real, still fails in `SFTDataset`'s padding divisor because the script builds its container without a model config (no layout), exactly as `--sft` fails there on `main`. A missing data source on `tools/prepare_cache.py` is rejected at validation instead of inside the builder.
4. `--sft --fim-data` and `--use-varlen-dataset --fim-data` keep their dataset class and every shared field, but the config is a plain `GPTDatasetConfig` instead of the FIM wrapper `pretrain_gpt` built around an SFT / varlen dataset (the packed datasets read no FIM field; AST check and identical mock samples under both configs in the tests).
5. The GPT providers use the run's tokenizer, bound once, instead of building a second tokenizer from `args` inside the provider; `pretrain(build_tokenizer=False)` with the stock GPT provider stops in the provider with a message naming `bind_tokenizer()` (no in-tree caller does this; `examples/mimo` passes `build_tokenizer=False` with its own provider).
6. The FIM flags without `--fim-data` are parsed as before but not stored: a plain `GPTDatasetConfig` has no FIM field, so `run_config.yaml` no longer records them.
7. The data-args and sequences files are read when the container is built, on every rank, instead of inside the provider; `pretrain_gpt` already ran its provider on every rank. `run_config.yaml` records the resolved blend.
8. `pretrain_hybrid_flex.py` forwards every data argument: `--multiple-validation-sets`, `--allow-ambiguous-pad-tokens`, `--dataloader-fast-cache-load`, `--dataloader-defer-npy-index-mmap` and `--per-dataset-sequences-path` take effect where its legacy factory ignored them (its only CI case, `hybrid_flextron_nightly_tp2_pp1_ep2_dgx_h100_1N8G`, passes `--data-path` alone); `--use-varlen-dataset` is rejected with an error where it silently built plain GPT data (its batch path has no varlen support). The layout mirrors still take Megatron Core's defaults there, as before, because the script builds its container without a model config.
9. `tools/prepare_cache.py` forwards the four fields its legacy factory left out (`inter_document_masking`, the two mock-dataset JSONs, `varlen_sbhd_validation`); none affects the cache it writes. `pretrain_hybrid.py` forwards `sft_mock_dataset_config_json`, read only by the mock SFT dataset it can now build.

Scope boundary: dataset construction is migrated; the data loaders and batch functions still read `args` (`pin_memory`, `persistent_workers` and `drop_last` are accepted in YAML / Python but the existing loaders keep their built-in values until the consumer migration, next PR), and `args.seq_length` keeps its readers (`cfg.data.dataset.sequence_length` is the sample length; the container checks that `model.seq_length`, the position-embedding capacity, covers it).

## Commits

1. `refactor(training): add GPTDatasetConfig, GPTFIMDatasetConfig, DataloaderConfig and DataConfig` (new module, class tests)
2. `refactor(training): add the data section to PretrainConfigContainer` (section, mirrors, data-parallel helper, factories, tokenizer binding)
3. `refactor(training): thread the config container to the dataset builders` (`data_config` keyword; reverted by commit 8)
4. `refactor(training): build GPT datasets from cfg.data in the providers` (the four entry points, ownership and provider tests, parser snapshot)
5. `refactor(training): share the GPT provider body and the legacy config wrapper` (`megatron/training/datasets/providers.py`, the helper in `argument_utils.py`, the scripts reduced to wrappers)
6. `refactor(training): keep only random_seed redeclared on GPTDatasetConfig` (the layout mirrors keep Core's fields and defaults, the prepared state is the bound tokenizer)
7. `refactor(training): make random_seed the data section's own setting` (filled from `--seed`, saved with the section; six mirrors remain, no field redeclared)
8. `refactor(training): drop the loader upgrade hook and the provider keyword` (`training.py` and the container loader back to `main`'s shape; the providers read the registered run config)
9. Merge of `main` `9e5aad0c6` (five conflicts, all in the data-section code, each resolution recorded in the merge commit's message; `is_dataset_built_on_rank`'s sequence-packing-scheduler rule from #8378 ported into the shared predicate)
10. `refactor(training): explicit cross-section checks for the data section` (one explicit check and one explicit write per field the container owns, `CONTAINER_WRITTEN_FIELDS`, Core's `safe_get_world_size`; the generic mirror machinery removed)
11. `refactor(core,training): Megatron Core's GPT dataset config validates itself` (Core's `validate()` replaces the GPT `__post_init__`, the builder validates, the FIM dataset moves to Core, the training subclass and its FIM subclass are gone, `DataConfig.bind_tokenizer` and `to_cfg_dict`)
12. `refactor(training): keep the scripts' rank predicate and accept a zero FIM rate` (the three CI findings on `09cced37a`: `tests/unit_tests/data/test_fim_dataset.py` builds the FIM config with `fim_spm_rate=0.0`, which Core had always accepted; `tests/unit_tests/data/test_get_batch.py` patches `get_args` and `core_transformer_config_from_args` and calls the scripts' `is_dataset_built_on_rank`, which commit 5 had made the shared predicate (the rule is split into `providers.dataset_built_on_rank`, explicit inputs, and `providers.is_dataset_built_on_rank`, the registered arguments); `tests/unit_tests/distributed/mfsdp_v1/test_mcore_fully_sharded_data_parallel.py` imitates `pretrain_gpt.py`'s main and now builds its container with the data section)
13. Merge of `main` `0a2f6eec5` (no conflicts; it brings #8414, which fixes the `dsa_layer_specs` import that failed `main`'s own Installation Test up to the previous merge base `9e5aad0c6`, and therefore this branch's)
14. `refactor(training): one rank predicate, patched where it reads` (commit 12 had put a copy of the predicate in each script for that test's patch targets; the scripts pass the shared predicate again and the test patches `megatron.training.global_vars.get_args` and `megatron.training.arguments.core_transformer_config_from_args`, which the predicate reads at call time)
15. `refactor(core): derived dataset-config values are properties; validate() asserts only` (the Bridge PIC's third review: `mock`, `split_matrix` and `token_dtype_code` are read-only properties of the sources, `split` and the bound tokenizer; `validate()` asserts only; `__post_init__` keeps the construction-time checks, which four Core subclasses and Megatron-Bridge call; `_resolve_sources` is gone; `sanitize_dataclass_config` drops the three names from older files)
16. `docs(core): say when BlendedMegatronDatasetConfig.__post_init__ can go` (a TODO on the method: Megatron-Bridge's `finalize()` calls it explicitly; the four Core subclasses that chain to it can drop their call in the same change)
17. `refactor(core): drop BlendedMegatronDatasetConfig.__post_init__` (nothing runs at construction; `DataConfig.validate()` runs Core's tokenizer-free checks; `MaskedWordPieceDatasetConfig` and `MultimodalDatasetConfig` drop their chained call; Megatron-Bridge's `finalize()` adapts in its bump PR)
18. `fix(core): mock data always uses the even split, as before` (the review of 2026-10-26: `split_matrix` is the even split whenever the config is mock, whatever `split` says, with `split` left as given; six CI functional cases run `--mock-data --split 949,50,1`)
19. `refactor(core,training): tokenizer-free dataset config checks run at cfg.validate()` (`validate_without_tokenizer()` on the blended, GPT and FIM configs; `validate()` runs it and then the tokenizer checks; `DataConfig.validate()` runs it, so a FIM section without a rate or a GPT section without its booleans fails at `cfg.validate()`, before runtime initialization; the asserts that can fire there name their field)
20. Merge of `main` `ed9c2c8c1` (#7047 dynamic context parallelism: the conflicts in `gpt_dataset.py`, `pretrain_gpt.py`, `pretrain_hybrid.py` and `tools/prepare_cache.py` resolved by keeping this PR's factory, provider and imports; `dynamic_context_parallel` joins `CONTAINER_WRITTEN_FIELDS`, the container reads either name against the model's flag, writes the canonical field and clears the deprecated `hybrid_context_parallel` alias; Core's `validate_without_tokenizer()` warns about the alias and rejects it next to the canonical flag without rewriting it)
21. `refactor(training): apply the datasets-group review to the data section` (`f55dce0ec`; the datasets review group's first pass of 2026-10-27, thirteen threads, no behaviour change: the family table is the module constant `DATASET_CLASSES` with `DATASET_FAMILIES` derived from it, the helpers are `dataset_type_from_family` / `dataset_family_from_type`, `DataConfig.dataset_build()` is `builder_inputs()`, the explicit-argument rank rule is `is_dataset_built_on_rank_explicit`, `argument_utils.py` imports `warn_rank_0` at the top and inlines its two single-use constants, `pretrain_hybrid_flex.py` checks `--use-varlen-dataset` once in its factory, the builder comment and the `hybrid_context_parallel` docstrings are reworded)
22. Merge of `main` `f77f360c9` (`c848be875`; #8391 builds the run's tokenizer from `cfg.tokenizer`: the conflicts in `megatron/training/config/__init__.py`, `megatron/training/global_vars.py`, `pretrain_gpt.py` and `pretrain_hybrid.py` are resolved by keeping this PR's imports and its removal of the legacy factories, adding `MultiModalTokenizerConfig` to the config package's exports and keeping the dataset-tokenizer binding after `main`'s new tokenizer construction; the shared legacy helper binds the run's registered tokenizer when no tokenizer is given, as `main`'s entry-point factories now do, and builds one from the arguments only when none is registered)

## Test evidence

- Unit: `tests/unit_tests/data/test_gpt_dataset_config.py` (Megatron Core: construction before the tokenizer exists, `validate()` asserting only, `mock` / `split_matrix` / `token_dtype_code` as read-only properties, the builder validating, the FIM config with a zero rate accepted and a missing one rejected), `tests/unit_tests/training/config/test_dataset_config.py`, `tests/unit_tests/training/test_dataset_ownership.py`, `tests/unit_tests/training/test_dataset_providers.py`, `tests/unit_tests/training/test_data_arguments.py`, plus `tests/unit_tests/data/test_gpt_dataset.py`, `tests/unit_tests/data/test_builder.py`, `tests/unit_tests/data/test_prepare_cache.py`, `tests/unit_tests/data/test_get_batch.py`, `tests/unit_tests/test_training.py` and `tests/unit_tests/training/test_initialization_lifecycle.py`: 592 passed per rank on two GPUs (head `c848be875`); the one failure, `test_rl_entrypoint_leaves_runtime_setup_to_pretrain`, needs `uvicorn` (absent from the image) and fails on `main` too. `pretrain_gpt`'s frozen factory of commit 438ef0025 is the oracle for every entry point: the bound and validated config equals that Core object field by field for every case, the dataset class and packedness match `pretrain_gpt`'s legacy provider, the fields the other three legacy factories left out are listed by a test, the mock datasets build identical samples through the real builder and receive `cfg.data.dataset` itself, each script's provider delegates to the shared body with the shared rank predicate (hybrid-flex with its own), which reads the registered arguments at call time, and each explicit cross-section check has a case. Three checks run only in CI (eight GPUs, or tokenizer assets that are not available locally): `tests/unit_tests/data/test_get_batch.py::test_packed_sequence_dataset_built_on_rank`, `tests/unit_tests/distributed/mfsdp_v1/test_mcore_fully_sharded_data_parallel.py::TestMegatronFSDPE2E::test_full_iteration_cuda_graph_e2e` and `tests/unit_tests/data/test_fim_dataset.py`; the CI run on `09cced37a` failed each of them and commits 12 and 13 fix them (the mfsdp test's data setup was also replayed locally on one rank: the provider builds the mock datasets from the data section).
- Unit gate (the training, data and argument suites on two GPUs, same selection on `main`): 1906 passed, 360 skipped, 6 failed per rank on this branch (head `c848be875`); `main` (`f77f360c9`) 1707 passed with the same 6 failures (the FIM tokenizer assets and the full-dataset-length asset are not available locally, `uvicorn` is missing from the image); the additional passes are the new tests.
- Corpus parity (every functional-test `model_config.yaml` parsed and validated on `main` and on this branch, head `c848be875`): 298 configs, 267 validated identically on both trees with every field equal and the dataset class the legacy provider selects (the documented implicit-mock difference included), 31 matched failures, 0 mismatches, no section rejected.
- Functional (two-GPU mock-data runs, deterministic settings, compared iteration by iteration with `main`, head `c848be875`): 9 of 9 comparisons identical over their windows (baseline repeatability, gpt, sft mock, varlen mock, pipeline parallel 2, mock data with `--split 949,50,1` against the baseline with the same flags and against the no-split baseline (`main` ignores the split for mock data; the pre-fix head `849a4804b` differed on every iteration), resume 1-10 and 11-20); the `run_config.yaml` written by the PR run loads, validates, finalizes and round-trips with the dataset class restored and the dataset section targeting Megatron Core's class, and a `main` file without the section loads with the loader-only default.
- Megatron-Bridge: its data and training-config unit tests against `main` and against this branch (head `c848be875`), compared per complete JUnit test id: 3 of 1535 ids differ, all failing on this branch inside `GPTDatasetConfig.finalize()` with `AttributeError` on the removed base `__post_init__` (298 failed on the branch against 295 on `main`); the one-line fix (`super(MCoreGPTDatasetConfig, self).validate()`) is Bridge's bump PR's, agreed with the Megatron-Bridge PIC, and with it applied to Bridge `d86a5c09b` the same suites against this branch are identical to `main` (0 differing ids of 1535, 295 failed and 1240 passed on both trees). The other ids are identical (1240 passed and 0 skipped on `main`; the `main` failures come from Bridge `d86a5c09b` pinning an older Megatron-LM, from optional dependencies missing in the image and, since `main` `f77f360c9`, from #8391's `sft_tokenizer_prompt_format` field clashing with Bridge's read-only property, which is why 25 of the 28 ids that differed before this merge now fail on both trees). This covers the Megatron Core change: Bridge's dataset config wrapper and its dataset builders run against the modified `megatron.core.datasets`.

## Contribution process

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests (existing `gpt` / `hybrid` functional suites cover the migrated providers; local mock-data runs above)
- [x] Not applicable: no GPU kernel is added or changed
- [x] I have added proper typing to my code
- [x] I have added relevant documentation (docstrings)
- [x] I have run `isort` on every edited file and `black` on the Megatron Core files and the tests (`tools/autoformat.sh` and `tools/check_copyright.py` pass)

+import logging
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Dict, Optional, Tuple
+
+import numpy as np
+
+from megatron.core.datasets.gpt_dataset import GPTDataset, GPTDatasetConfig
+from megatron.core.datasets.indexed_dataset import IndexedDataset
+from megatron.core.datasets.utils import Split
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+_FIM_TOKEN_KEYS = ("prefix", "middle", "suffix", "pad", "eod")
+
+
+@dataclass
+class GPTFIMDatasetConfig(GPTDatasetConfig):
+    """Configuration object for Megatron Core GPT FIM datasets"""
+
+    fim_rate: float = None
+    """Probability to convert a training sample into a FIM format"""
+
+    fim_spm_rate: float = None
+    """Probability that the a FIM sample uses the SPM format over the PSM format"""
+
+    fim_extra_tokens: Dict = None
+    """FIM extra tokens. Should consist of prefix, middle, suffix, PAD, and EOD tokens."""
+
+    fim_split_sample: Optional[str] = None
+    """String around which to split the sample for FIM"""
+
+    fim_fragment_rate: Optional[float] = None
+    """Rate of FIM on each fragment when split_sample is not None"""
+
+    fim_no_prefix: Optional[str] = None
+    """Do not apply FIM to fragments that start with this prefix"""
+
+    def validate_without_tokenizer(self) -> None:
+        """The GPT checks that need no tokenizer, then the FIM ones, which need none either: both
+        rates and the five extra tokens must be given (a rate of 0.0 is a value; ``validate_args``
+        checks the same for ``--fim-data``). ``validate()`` runs this before the tokenizer checks.
+        """
+        super().validate_without_tokenizer()
+        assert self.fim_rate is not None, "fim_rate should be specified."
+        assert self.fim_spm_rate is not None, "fim_spm_rate should be specified."
+        assert self.fim_extra_tokens is not None and all(
+            self.fim_extra_tokens.get(key) is not None for key in _FIM_TOKEN_KEYS
+        ), (
+            "FIM extra tokens should be specified: fim_extra_tokens needs the keys "
+            f"{_FIM_TOKEN_KEYS}."
+        )
+
+
+class GPTFIMDataset(GPTDataset):
+    """The GPT dataset with fill-in-the-middle preprocessing
+
+    Args:
+        indexed_dataset (IndexedDataset): The IndexedDataset around which to build the
+        MegatronDataset
+
+        indexed_indices (np.ndarray): The set of the documents indices to expose
+
+        num_samples (int): The number of samples to draw from the indexed dataset
+
+        index_split (Split): The indexed_indices Split
+
+        config (GPTFIMDatasetConfig): The GPT-specific container for all config sourced parameters
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        indexed_dataset: IndexedDataset,
+        dataset_path: str,
+        indexed_indices: np.ndarray,
+        num_samples: int,
+        index_split: Split,
+        config: GPTFIMDatasetConfig,
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__(
+            indexed_dataset, dataset_path, indexed_indices, num_samples, index_split, config
+        )
+
+        self.np_rng = np.random.RandomState(seed=self.config.random_seed)
+        logger.info(f"Initialized FIM RNG with seed = {self.config.random_seed}")
+        # get FIM params
+        self.fim_rate = self.config.fim_rate
+        self.fim_spm_rate = self.config.fim_spm_rate
+        self.fragment_fim_rate = self.config.fim_fragment_rate
+        fim_split_sample = self.config.fim_split_sample
+        self.no_fim_prefix = self.config.fim_no_prefix
+        if fim_split_sample:
+            fim_split_sample_ids = self.config.tokenizer._tokenizer.tokens_to_ids(fim_split_sample)
+            assert isinstance(fim_split_sample_ids, int) or len(fim_split_sample_ids) == 1
+            self.fim_split_sample = (
+                fim_split_sample_ids
+                if isinstance(fim_split_sample_ids, int)
+                else fim_split_sample_ids[0]
+            )
+        else:
+            self.fim_split_sample = None
+
+        # get extra tokens ids
+        fim_tokens = self.config.fim_extra_tokens
+        fim_tokens = [
+            fim_tokens["prefix"],
+            fim_tokens["middle"],
+            fim_tokens["suffix"],
+            fim_tokens["pad"],
+            fim_tokens["eod"],
+        ]
+        fim_tokens_ids = self.config.tokenizer._tokenizer.tokens_to_ids(fim_tokens)
+        (
+            self.prefix_tok_id,
+            self.middle_tok_id,
+            self.suffix_tok_id,
+            self.pad_tok_id,
+            self.eod_tok_id,
+        ) = fim_tokens_ids
+
+    def _query_document_sample_shuffle_indices(
+        self, idx: int
+    ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, list]:
+        """Get the text (token ids) and document ids for a given index
+
+        Args:
+            idx (int): The index into the dataset
+
+        Returns:
+            Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, list]: The text ids, document ids,
+                and per-document token counts.
+        """
+        # Do the shuffle mapping
+        idx = self.shuffle_index[idx]
+
+        # Get the beginning and end documents and offsets
+        doc_index_beg, doc_index_beg_offset = self.sample_index[idx]
+        doc_index_end, doc_index_end_offset = self.sample_index[idx + 1]
+
+        document_ids = []
+        sample_parts = []
+
+        # Sample spans a single document
+        if doc_index_beg == doc_index_end:
+            # Add the document id
+            document_ids.append(self.document_index[doc_index_beg])
+
+            # Add the entire sample
+            sample_parts.append(
+                self.dataset.get(
+                    self.document_index[doc_index_beg],
+                    offset=doc_index_beg_offset,
+                    length=doc_index_end_offset - doc_index_beg_offset + 1,
+                )
+            )
+
+        # Sample spans multiple documents
+        else:
+            for i in range(doc_index_beg, doc_index_end + 1):
+                # Add the document id
+                document_ids.append(self.document_index[i])
+
+                # Add the sample part
+                offset = 0 if i > doc_index_beg else doc_index_beg_offset
+                length = None if i < doc_index_end else doc_index_end_offset + 1
+                sample_parts.append(
+                    self.dataset.get(self.document_index[i], offset=offset, length=length)
+                )
+
+        sample = np.concatenate(sample_parts)
+
+        sample_len = sample.shape[0]
+        segment_breaks = np.argwhere(sample == self.eod_tok_id)
+
+        if segment_breaks.shape != (0, 1):  # then there is an EOD token in this example
+            curr_start_position = 0
+            new_samples = []
+            for loc in np.nditer(segment_breaks):
+                # Only permute non-empty segments.
+                if loc - curr_start_position > 0:
+                    # permute {prefix, suffix, middle} or {suffix, prefix, middle}
+                    permuted = self._fim_split_and_permute_sequence(sample[curr_start_position:loc])
+                    new_samples += [permuted, [self.eod_tok_id]]
+
+                curr_start_position = loc + 1  # jump over the EOD token
+            # Permute the segment after the last EOD
+            permuted = self._fim_split_and_permute_sequence(sample[curr_start_position:])
+            new_samples.append(permuted)
+
+            sample = np.concatenate(new_samples)
+        else:
+            sample = self._fim_split_and_permute_sequence(sample)
+
+        diff = sample.shape[0] - sample_len
+        if diff > 0:  # too long
+            sample = sample[:sample_len]
+        elif diff < 0:  # too short
+            sample = np.concatenate([sample, np.full((-1 * diff), self.pad_tok_id)])
+
+        assert sample.shape[0] == sample_len
+
+        return (
+            np.array(sample, dtype=np.int64),
+            np.array(document_ids, dtype=np.int64),
+            [sample_len],
+        )
+
+    def _fim_permute_sequence(self, sequence, rate):
+        return self._permute(
+            sequence,
+            rate,
+            self.fim_spm_rate,
+            self.config.tokenizer,
+            truncate_or_pad=False,
+            suffix_tok_id=self.suffix_tok_id,
+            prefix_tok_id=self.prefix_tok_id,
+            middle_tok_id=self.middle_tok_id,
+            pad_tok_id=self.pad_tok_id,
+            no_fim_prefix=self.no_fim_prefix,
+        )
+
+    def _fim_split_and_permute_sequence(self, sequence):
+        """
+        If self.fim_split_sample is not None, split the sequence.
+        Then apply FIM on the fragments, or the whole sequence if self.fim_split_sample is None.
+        """
+        if self.fim_split_sample is None:
+            return self._fim_permute_sequence(sequence, self.fim_rate)
+        # fim_split_sample is set: split the sample on this token and permute each fragment
+        # separately.
+        # Typically, if each sample is a repository, then we split again on the file level.
+        # Each fragment is a file, and we permute the files.
+        fragment_breaks = np.argwhere(sequence == self.fim_split_sample)
+        if fragment_breaks.shape == (0, 1):
+            # no split token in this sample
+            return self._fim_permute_sequence(sequence, self.fim_rate)
+        if not self.np_rng.binomial(1, self.fim_rate):
+            # don't do FIM preproc
+            return sequence
+        # Do FIM on each fragment
+        curr_start_position = 0
+        new_samples = []
+        for loc in np.nditer(fragment_breaks):
+            if loc - curr_start_position > 0:
+                permuted = self._fim_permute_sequence(
+                    sequence[curr_start_position:loc], self.fragment_fim_rate
+                )
+                new_samples += [permuted, [self.fim_split_sample]]
+            curr_start_position = loc + 1  # Jump over the split token
+        # Permute the segment after the last split token
+        permuted = self._fim_permute_sequence(
+            sequence[curr_start_position:], self.fragment_fim_rate
+        )
+        new_samples.append(permuted)
+
+        return np.concatenate(new_samples)
+
+    def _permute(
+        self,
+        sample,
+        fim_rate,
+        fim_spm_rate,
+        tokenizer,
+        truncate_or_pad=True,
+        suffix_tok_id=None,
+        prefix_tok_id=None,
+        middle_tok_id=None,
+        pad_tok_id=None,
+        no_fim_prefix=None,
+    ):
+        """
+        Take in a sample (np array w/ size (0,chunklength)) and perform a FIM transformation on it.
+        Maintain the same sample length (if transform creates a few extra tokens, drop them).
+        """
+        if self.np_rng.binomial(1, fim_rate):  # sample bernoulli dist
+
+            # Use remove_special_tokens=True so character-level boundaries and re-tokenization
+            # are consistent; otherwise ids_to_text(..., None) keeps special tokens when
+            # include_special_tokens=True, changing contents and breaking e.g. split_sample.
+            contents = tokenizer._tokenizer.ids_to_text(sample, remove_special_tokens=True)
+
+            # Do not apply FIM if the sample starts with no_fim_prefix

+                return sample
+
+            try:
+                # A boundary can be =0 (prefix will be empty)
+                # a boundary can be =len(contents) (suffix will be empty)
+                # The two boundaries can be equal (middle will be empty)
+                boundaries = list(self.np_rng.randint(low=0, high=len(contents) + 1, size=2))
+                boundaries.sort()
+            except ValueError as e:
+                logger.error("%s %s", len(contents), contents)
+                logger.error(e)

+            suffix = contents[boundaries[1] :]

+"""The ``data`` section of ``PretrainConfigContainer``: Megatron Core's GPT dataset config, the loader
+settings and the dataset class.
+
+``DataConfig.dataset`` is ``megatron.core.datasets.gpt_dataset.GPTDatasetConfig`` itself (or its FIM
+subclass), the object ``BlendedMegatronDatasetBuilder`` consumes, constructed from the arguments or
+a YAML file before the tokenizer exists: nothing runs at construction, Core's checks that need no
+tokenizer (``validate_without_tokenizer()``) run at ``cfg.validate()``, and the complete
+``validate()``, which needs the tokenizer, runs in ``DataConfig.bind_tokenizer`` once the runtime
+services bind the run's tokenizer (the builder runs it again before building).
+``random_seed`` is Core's required constructor argument, filled from ``--seed`` by the factory and
+saved with the section. Seven Core fields are owned by other container sections (the parallel
+layout with its deprecated ``hybrid_context_parallel`` alias, the validation flags): the container
+writes them at ``finalize()`` (``CONTAINER_WRITTEN_FIELDS``) and they are not serialized with the
+section.
+
+``DataConfig`` groups the dataset config, the ``DataloaderConfig`` and ``dataset_type``, the dataset
+class the builder instantiates (``GPTDataset``, ``MockGPTDataset``, ``GPTFIMDataset``, ...). One rule
+serves every GPT entry point: the args-to-config factory forwards every data argument, the class
+follows the family flags, and the provider hands ``cfg.data.dataset`` to the builder unchanged.
+Entry points with their own data pipeline carry a loader-only section (``dataset is None``) and
+nothing here runs for them.
+"""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field, fields
+from typing import Any
+
+from megatron.core.datasets.gpt_dataset import GPTDataset, GPTDatasetConfig, MockGPTDataset
+from megatron.core.datasets.gpt_fim_dataset import GPTFIMDataset, GPTFIMDatasetConfig
+from megatron.training.datasets.sft_dataset import MockSFTDataset, SFTDataset
+from megatron.training.datasets.varlen_dataset import MockVarlenDataset, VarlenDataset
+
+DATALOADER_TYPES = ("single", "cyclic", "external")
+# Family -> (dataset class, mock dataset class or None): the legacy family flags select the class
+# and DataConfig.validate() checks the class against the config.
+DATASET_CLASSES: dict[str, tuple[type, type | None]] = {
+    "gpt": (GPTDataset, MockGPTDataset),
+    "fim": (GPTFIMDataset, None),
+    "varlen": (VarlenDataset, MockVarlenDataset),
+    "sft": (SFTDataset, MockSFTDataset),
+}
+DATASET_FAMILIES = tuple(DATASET_CLASSES)
+
+# Fields of the dataset config that other container sections own: the parallel layout (the model
+# config) and the validation flags (the validation config). PretrainConfigContainer writes them at
+# finalize(), the container-oriented factory leaves them unset and the section serializes without
+# them: they are recorded once, in their owning sections. hybrid_context_parallel is the deprecated
+# alias of dynamic_context_parallel (#7047): the container folds it into the canonical field and
+# clears it, so it is neither serialized nor left set.
+CONTAINER_WRITTEN_FIELDS = (
+    "data_parallel_size",
+    "context_parallel_size",
+    "sequence_parallel_size",
+    "dynamic_context_parallel",
+    "hybrid_context_parallel",
+    "multiple_validation_sets",
+    "full_validation",
+)
+
+
+@dataclass(kw_only=True)
+class DataloaderConfig:
+    """Settings for building torch DataLoaders on top of a dataset."""
+
+    dataloader_type: str | None = None
+    """Single pass vs multiple pass data loader. 'external' passes the dataset through unchanged.
+    Unset selects 'single'."""
+
+    num_workers: int = 2
+    """Dataloader number of workers."""
+
+    data_sharding: bool = True
+    """Shard the dataset per data-parallel rank before shuffling (cyclic sampler only)."""
+
+    pin_memory: bool = True
+    """Pin host memory in the torch DataLoader. Declared only for now: the training loop keeps its
+    built-in value until the loader consumers read this config."""
+
+    persistent_workers: bool = True
+    """Keep DataLoader workers alive between epochs. Forced to False when num_workers == 0. Declared
+    only for now: the training loop keeps its built-in value until the loader consumers read it."""
+
+    drop_last: bool = True
+    """Drop the last incomplete micro-batch. Declared only for now: the training loop keeps its
+    built-in value until the loader consumers read this config."""
+
+    def validate(self) -> None:
+        """Check the loader settings without mutation."""
+        if self.dataloader_type is not None and self.dataloader_type not in DATALOADER_TYPES:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"dataloader_type must be one of {DATALOADER_TYPES}, got {self.dataloader_type!r}."
+            )
+        if self.num_workers < 0:
+            raise ValueError(f"num_workers must be non-negative, got {self.num_workers}.")
+
+    def finalize(self) -> None:
+        """Apply the loader defaults (idempotent): unset type -> 'single', no workers -> no
+        persistent workers."""
+        if self.dataloader_type is None:
+            self.dataloader_type = "single"
+        if self.num_workers == 0 and self.persistent_workers:
+            self.persistent_workers = False
+
+
+def dataset_type_from_family(family: str, mock: bool) -> type | None:
+    """The dataset class of a family, or its mock class (``None`` when the family has none); the
+    inverse of ``dataset_family_from_type``."""
+    if family not in DATASET_CLASSES:
+        raise ValueError(f"dataset family must be one of {DATASET_FAMILIES}, got {family!r}.")
+    real, mock_class = DATASET_CLASSES[family]
+    return mock_class if mock else real
+
+
+def dataset_family_from_type(dataset_type: Any) -> tuple[str, bool]:
+    """``(family, is_mock)`` of one of the seven supported dataset classes; the inverse of
+    ``dataset_type_from_family``."""
+    for family, (real, mock_class) in DATASET_CLASSES.items():
+        if dataset_type is real:
+            return family, False
+        if mock_class is not None and dataset_type is mock_class:
+            return family, True
+    known = sorted(
+        cls.__name__ for pair in DATASET_CLASSES.values() for cls in pair if cls is not None
+    )
+    raise ValueError(
+        f"dataset_type must be one of the dataset classes {known} (in YAML: "
+        "{_target_: <module>.<class>, _call_: false}), got "
+        f"{getattr(dataset_type, '__name__', dataset_type)!r}."
+    )
+
+
+def has_data_source(dataset: GPTDatasetConfig) -> bool:
+    """Whether a blend is declared: the inverse of Megatron Core's ``mock``."""
+    return not dataset.mock
+
+
+def is_packed_sequence(dataset_type: type, dataset: GPTDatasetConfig) -> bool:
+    """Packed (THD) samples: built on every pipeline stage, and get_batch expects cu_seqlens."""
+    family, _mock = dataset_family_from_type(dataset_type)
+    if family == "sft":
+        return True
+    if family == "varlen":
+        return not dataset.varlen_sbhd_validation
+    return False
+
+
+def resolve_dataset_class(
+    dataset: GPTDatasetConfig | None, dataset_type: type | None
+) -> type | None:
+    """The dataset class the config entails, or the given one checked against the config.
+
+    Read-only: ``DataConfig.validate()`` calls it and ``DataConfig.finalize()`` commits its result.
+    With no class given, a ``GPTFIMDatasetConfig`` with a source resolves to ``GPTFIMDataset``, a
+    plain config with a source to ``GPTDataset`` and a plain config without one to
+    ``MockGPTDataset``; sft and varlen share the plain config class and are always explicit. An
+    explicit class must match the config (mock without a source, real with one, the FIM class with
+    the FIM config); nothing is silently rewritten.
+    """
+    if dataset is None:
+        if dataset_type is not None:
+            raise ValueError("dataset_type needs a dataset: cfg.data.dataset is None.")
+        return None
+    source = has_data_source(dataset)
+    config_family = "fim" if isinstance(dataset, GPTFIMDatasetConfig) else None
+    if dataset_type is None:
+        family = config_family or "gpt"
+        if source:
+            return dataset_type_from_family(family, mock=False)
+        mock_class = dataset_type_from_family(family, mock=True)
+        if mock_class is None:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"No data source is declared and there is no mock dataset for the {family} "
+                "family; declare blend or blend_per_split."
+            )
+        return mock_class
+    family, mock = dataset_family_from_type(dataset_type)
+    real, mock_class = DATASET_CLASSES[family]
+    if mock and source:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{dataset_type.__name__} is a mock dataset and takes no data source; drop blend / "
+            f"blend_per_split or select {real.__name__}."
+        )
+    if not mock and not source:
+        if mock_class is not None:
+            hint = f"select {mock_class.__name__} for mock data"
+        else:
+            hint = f"there is no mock dataset for the {family} family"
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{dataset_type.__name__} needs a data source (blend or blend_per_split); {hint}."
+        )
+    if (family == "fim") != (config_family == "fim"):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "GPTFIMDataset and GPTFIMDatasetConfig go together: the FIM fields live on that config "
+            f"class and only GPTFIMDataset reads them (got {dataset_type.__name__} with "
+            f"{type(dataset).__name__})."
+        )

+        raise ValueError("varlen_sbhd_validation requires real data (VarlenDataset, not its mock).")
+    return dataset_type
+
+
+@dataclass(kw_only=True)
+class DataConfig:
+    """``PretrainConfigContainer.data``: the dataset config, the loader settings, the dataset class.
+
+    ``dataset is None`` is the loader-only section of entry points with their own data pipeline;
+    nothing dataset-related is validated, bound or built for it.
+    """
+
+    dataset: GPTDatasetConfig | None = None
+    """Megatron Core's GPT dataset config (or ``GPTFIMDatasetConfig``), handed to
+    ``BlendedMegatronDatasetBuilder`` as is."""
+
+    dataloader: DataloaderConfig = field(default_factory=DataloaderConfig)
+    """Loader settings."""
+
+    dataset_type: type | None = None
+    """The dataset class the builder instantiates (``GPTDataset``, ``MockGPTDataset``,
+    ``GPTFIMDataset``, ``SFTDataset``, ``MockSFTDataset``, ``VarlenDataset``, ``MockVarlenDataset``).
+    Resolved at ``finalize()`` when unset. In YAML: ``{_target_: <module>.<class>, _call_: false}``."""
+
+    def validate(self) -> None:
+        """Check the loader settings and the class / config agreement; no mutation.
+
+        Megatron Core's checks that need no tokenizer (``validate_without_tokenizer()``: the blend /
+        split rules, the GPT booleans, the FIM rates and tokens) run here too, so a YAML or Python
+        section fails at ``cfg.validate()``, before runtime initialization; the checks that need the
+        tokenizer run in ``bind_tokenizer()`` and in the builder.
+        """
+        self.dataloader.validate()
+        if self.dataset is not None:
+            self.dataset.validate_without_tokenizer()
+        resolve_dataset_class(self.dataset, self.dataset_type)
+
+    def finalize(self) -> None:
+        """Apply the loader defaults and commit the resolved dataset class (idempotent)."""
+        self.dataloader.finalize()
+        if self.dataset is not None:
+            self.dataset_type = resolve_dataset_class(self.dataset, self.dataset_type)
+
+    def bind_tokenizer(self, tokenizer: Any) -> None:
+        """Bind the run's tokenizer to the dataset config and run Megatron Core's ``validate()``.
+
+        The step between ``finalize()`` and the first build: ``initialize_runtime_services`` does it
+        once the tokenizer exists. Idempotent for the same tokenizer; another tokenizer is an error
+        (the datasets built from this config share it by reference: build a new config for a
+        differently configured run). Nothing happens for a loader-only section.
+        """
+        if self.dataset is None:
+            return

+            raise ValueError("bind_tokenizer() needs a tokenizer.")

+            self.dataset.tokenizer = tokenizer

+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "cfg.data.dataset is already bound to another tokenizer; build a new config for a "
+                "differently configured run."
+            )

+
+    def builder_inputs(self) -> tuple[type, GPTDatasetConfig, bool]:
+        """``(dataset class, dataset config with its tokenizer, is_packed_sequence)`` for the
+        builder."""
+        if self.dataset is None or self.dataset_type is None:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "cfg.data carries no dataset to build: construct the container with "
+                "data_cfg=gpt_data_config_from_args(args) and finalize it."
+            )
+        if self.dataset.tokenizer is None:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "cfg.data.dataset has no tokenizer bound: initialize_megatron() with "
+                "build_tokenizer=True binds the run's tokenizer, or call "
+                "cfg.data.bind_tokenizer(tokenizer)."
+            )
+        return self.dataset_type, self.dataset, is_packed_sequence(self.dataset_type, self.dataset)
+
+    def to_cfg_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        """Serialize the section.
+
+        The dataset config is written with every constructor field except the tokenizer and the
+        fields other sections own (``CONTAINER_WRITTEN_FIELDS``, recorded once, in their owning
+        sections); Megatron Core's derived values (``mock``, ``split_matrix``, ``token_dtype_code``)
+        are read-only properties, not fields, and are never written.
+        """
+        from megatron.training.config.container import ConfigContainerBase
+
+        convert = ConfigContainerBase._convert_value_to_dict
+        dataset = None
+        if self.dataset is not None:
+            cls = type(self.dataset)
+            dataset = {"_target_": f"{cls.__module__}.{cls.__qualname__}"}

+        }

+"""The GPT dataset provider shared by the GPT entry points.
+
+``build_gpt_datasets`` is the body of ``train_valid_test_datasets_provider`` in ``pretrain_gpt.py``,
+``pretrain_hybrid.py`` and ``megatron/elastification/pretrain_hybrid_flex.py``: it takes ``cfg.data``
+(the dataset config bound to the run's tokenizer, the loader settings and the dataset class)
+and hands the dataset config to ``BlendedMegatronDatasetBuilder`` as is. Each script keeps a
+``train_valid_test_datasets_provider`` of the legacy shape that calls it with its rank predicate:
+``is_dataset_built_on_rank_explicit`` below is the GPT and hybrid rule with its inputs spelled out
+(a packed dataset is built on every pipeline stage, the others on the first and last stages and on
+the multi-token-prediction ranks); ``is_dataset_built_on_rank`` applies it to the registered
+arguments and is the predicate ``pretrain_gpt.py`` and ``pretrain_hybrid.py`` pass; hybrid-flex
+passes its own.
+"""
+
+from functools import partial
+from typing import Any, Callable, Optional
+
+from megatron.core import mpu
+from megatron.core.datasets.blended_megatron_dataset_builder import BlendedMegatronDatasetBuilder
+from megatron.core.transformer.multi_token_prediction import mtp_on_this_rank
+
+
+def is_dataset_built_on_rank_explicit(
+    vp_stage: Optional[int],
+    is_packed_sequence: bool,
+    *,
+    sequence_packing_scheduler: Optional[str],
+    pipeline_model_parallel_layout: Any,
+    mtp_num_layers: Optional[int],
+) -> bool:
+    """Whether the dataset should be built on the current rank: the GPT and hybrid rule, with the
+    run's inputs given explicitly (``is_dataset_built_on_rank`` reads them from the arguments).
+
+    Only tensor-parallel rank 0 builds. A sequence-packing scheduler or packed dataset builds
+    on every pipeline stage; the others on the first and last stages and on the
+    multi-token-prediction ranks.
+    """
+    from megatron.training.utils import is_first_or_last_pipeline_stage
+
+    if mpu.get_tensor_model_parallel_rank() != 0:
+        return False
+    if is_packed_sequence or sequence_packing_scheduler is not None:
+        # The sequence-packing scheduler runs on every PP stage and reads its input there.
+        return True
+    return is_first_or_last_pipeline_stage(vp_stage) or mtp_on_this_rank(
+        layout=pipeline_model_parallel_layout,
+        mtp_num_layers=mtp_num_layers,
+        ignore_virtual=False,
+        vp_stage=vp_stage,
+    )
+
+
+def is_dataset_built_on_rank(
+    vp_stage: Optional[int] = None, is_packed_sequence: bool = False
+) -> bool:
+    """``is_dataset_built_on_rank_explicit`` applied to the registered arguments: the predicate
+    ``pretrain_gpt.py`` and ``pretrain_hybrid.py`` pass, and the default of ``build_gpt_datasets``.
+    The arguments and the transformer config are read at call time from
+    ``megatron.training.global_vars`` and ``megatron.training.arguments``, which is where tests
+    patch them."""
+    from megatron.training.arguments import core_transformer_config_from_args
+    from megatron.training.global_vars import get_args
+
+    args = get_args()
+    config = core_transformer_config_from_args(args)
+    return is_dataset_built_on_rank_explicit(
+        vp_stage,
+        is_packed_sequence,
+        sequence_packing_scheduler=args.sequence_packing_scheduler,
+        pipeline_model_parallel_layout=config.pipeline_model_parallel_layout,
+        mtp_num_layers=config.mtp_num_layers,
+    )
+
+
+def build_gpt_datasets(
+    train_val_test_num_samples,
+    vp_stage: Optional[int] = None,
+    *,
+    data_config: Any = None,
+    built_on_rank: Optional[Callable[..., bool]] = None,
+):
+    """Build the train, validation and test datasets from ``cfg.data``.
+
+    Args:
+        train_val_test_num_samples: the number of samples for the train, validation and test
+            splits.
+        vp_stage: the virtual pipeline stage the datasets are built for.
+        data_config: ``cfg.data``; the registered run config's when omitted (the scripts'
+            providers), given explicitly by tests and direct callers.
+        built_on_rank: the rank predicate, called with ``vp_stage`` and ``is_packed_sequence``;
+            ``is_dataset_built_on_rank`` (the GPT and hybrid rule) when omitted.
+    """
+    from megatron.training.global_vars import get_run_config
+    from megatron.training.utils import print_rank_0
+
+    if data_config is None:
+        data_config = get_run_config().data
+    if built_on_rank is None:
+        built_on_rank = is_dataset_built_on_rank
+    dataset_type, config, is_packed_sequence = data_config.builder_inputs()
+
+    print_rank_0("> building train, validation, and test datasets for GPT ...")
+
+    train_ds, valid_ds, test_ds = BlendedMegatronDatasetBuilder(
+        dataset_type,
+        train_val_test_num_samples,
+        partial(built_on_rank, vp_stage=vp_stage, is_packed_sequence=is_packed_sequence),
+        config,
+    ).build()
+
+    print_rank_0("> finished creating GPT datasets ...")
+
+    return train_ds, valid_ds, test_ds

+def _full_parser():

+    actions = {}
+    for action in parser._actions:
+        if action.dest == "help":
+            continue
+        if action.dest in LEGACY:
+            assert action.dest not in actions, f"{action.dest} is registered twice"

+    return actions
+
+
+def _describe(action):
+    return dict(
+        option_strings=list(action.option_strings),
+        default=action.default,
+        nargs=action.nargs,
+        type=None if action.type is None else getattr(action.type, "__name__", repr(action.type)),
+        choices=None if action.choices is None else list(action.choices),
+        action=type(action).__name__,
+        required=action.required,
+        const=action.const,
+    )
+
+
+def test_every_legacy_data_argument_is_unchanged():
+    actions = _actions_by_dest(_full_parser())
+    for dest, legacy in LEGACY.items():

+            seen[option] = action.dest

+    ``project_dataset_type_into_args``) and the config factories agree: an explicit ``dataset_type``

+    over ``fim``, as today's providers choose); any other disagreement is an error, a combination
+    that could not be written before. ``--sft`` with ``--use-varlen-dataset`` is rejected as
+    ``validate_args`` does. Several alias flags warn once (``warn=True``) where today the losers
+    are silently ignored.
+    """
+    explicit = getattr(args, "dataset_type", None)
+    aliases = [
+        family for _flag, (dest, family) in LEGACY_ALIAS_FLAGS.items() if getattr(args, dest, False)

+    if "sft" in aliases and "varlen" in aliases:

+            "packed-sequence dataset family. Pick one."

inline_comments.body:
It is the input bundle for converting the dataset declaration into the runtime Megatron Core config: the eight constructor inputs the dataset section does not own. The tokenizer and `data_parallel_size` come from runtime initialization; `random_seed` is `cfg.rng.seed`, the CP/SP sizes are `cfg.model.transformer` (#8234), the validation flags are `cfg.validation` (#8149). Megatron Core has them as fields because it has no container; the declarative class redeclares them as `None` so they are optional at declaration time. Passing their resolved values keeps `to_core_config()` independent of `args`, of globals and of either repository's container layout, and nothing runtime is ever written into `cfg.dataset`.

During the migration, `build_dataset_runtime_context` in `training.py` supplies the layout and validation values that `args` still owns; once those sections are authoritative, that adapter reads `cfg` and the converter's inputs stay the same. Bridge builds the same context from its own container with its own seed precedence (declared dataset seed over `rng.seed`), which a copy persisted in `cfg.dataset` could not express. Explicit keyword arguments could carry the same contract; the dataclass keeps the provider interface typed and compact.

The split is between the editable declaration in `cfg.dataset` and Megatron Core's runtime config, which needs a tokenizer instance to construct and eagerly derives `split_matrix` / `mock` / `token_dtype_code`. `to_core_config()` is the only place they meet and the Megatron Core API is untouched; making the core class declarative would be a core API change for every dataset consumer, which this series avoids.

I agree the identical name obscures that split: `pretrain_gpt.py` itself imported the core class as `GPTDatasetConfig` a few lines from the provider parameter that holds the declarative one. For now (1c41f7e3f) the class docstring spells out the two roles and the entry points that see both import the core class as `MCoreGPTDatasetConfig`. Two options, both cheap now and not later (once `_target_` strings are persisted, a rename needs permanent aliases): keep the name as is, or rename the declarative class now, for example `GPTDatasetSetupConfig` (the `InferenceSetupConfig` / `InferenceConfig` precedent in this container) or `GPTDatasetSpec`. Bridge's public `megatron.bridge.training.config.GPTDatasetConfig` stays either way. I lean to keeping the name so that both repositories spell the declarative class the same at the merge, but it is your call; tell me which and I will do it in this PR.

+    that could not be written before. ``--sft`` with ``--use-varlen-dataset`` is rejected as
+    ``validate_args`` does. Several alias flags warn once (``warn=True``) where today the losers
+    are silently ignored.

+    aliases = [

+        raise ValueError(
+            f"--dataset-type {explicit} contradicts the legacy flag(s) selecting {aliases}."
+        )
+    if warn and len(aliases) > 1:
+        _warn(f"{aliases} were all requested; '{aliases[0]}' wins, as in today's providers.")
+    if explicit is not None:
+        return explicit
+    return legacy or "gpt"

+    ``args.sft`` / ``args.use_varlen_dataset`` / ``args.fim_data``: ``--dataset-type varlen`` then
+    auto-selects the packing scheduler, collates and batches exactly like ``--use-varlen-dataset``.
+    Flags the user passed are never cleared, so legacy namespaces are unchanged field by field, and
+    calling this again (or ``dataset_type_from_args``) returns the same family.
+    """
+    resolved = dataset_type_from_args(args)
+    args.dataset_type = resolved
+    for _flag, (dest, family) in LEGACY_ALIAS_FLAGS.items():
+        if family == resolved:
+            setattr(args, dest, True)
+    return resolved

+    """YAML gives lists; Megatron Core expects a (prefixes, weights) tuple."""
+    if blend is None:
+        return None
+    prefixes, weights = blend
+    return (list(prefixes), None if weights is None else list(weights))
+
+
+@dataclass(kw_only=True)
+class GPTDatasetConfig(MCoreGPTDatasetConfig, DataloaderConfig):

Done in a3493d17a: the eleven `fim_*` fields, the FIM validation and the FIM conversion branch now live on `GPTFIMDatasetConfig`. A plain `GPTDatasetConfig` has no FIM fields and cannot declare `dataset_type="fim"`, and the subclass declares no other family (checked at validation and again at conversion, since the tools convert without a container). `--fim-data` / `--dataset-type fim` build the subclass; the data group is generated from it, so every flag, dest and default is unchanged and `--dataset-type` keeps its `None` parser default. The hybrid / hybrid-flex / prepare_cache "build the plain GPT family" projections go through a new `as_family("gpt")`, which returns a base-class copy and leaves the request untouched, and `to_core_config()` is split into a shared `_core_kwargs()` plus two thin constructors, so each runtime object is built once from one set of keywords.

Gates re-run on this head: the focused suites (359 per rank), the two-GPU unit selection (1676 passed, the same six environment failures as `main`), corpus parity (308/308 identical; the two FIM configs resolve to the subclass), the functional gate (all ten comparisons identical) and Bridge's tests (identical per test id). One consequence, added to the description as the fifth documented difference: the FIM flags without `--fim-data` are no longer stored on the plain declaration (the build ignored them before, so the dataset is unchanged; `run_config.yaml` just stops recording them). SFT and varlen stay selector values for now, as discussed.

+
+    reset_attention_mask: bool = False
+    """Reset self attention mask after end-of-document token."""
+
+    eod_mask_loss: bool = False

+
+    allow_ambiguous_pad_tokens: bool = False

+    pad token incorrectly shares the same id with other special tokens in the tokenizer. Note that
+    this argument has no effect when the tokenizer correctly provides a unique id for the pad.

+    are truly pad. If instead this argument is set, the training flow will treat all tokens that
+    share the same id as the pad token as true pad tokens, potentially causing severe training
+    instability."""
+
+    data_parallel_size: int | None = None

+                f"dataloader_type must be one of {DATALOADER_TYPES}, got {self.dataloader_type!r}."
+            )
+
+    def finalize(self) -> None:
+        """Apply the loader spelling normalization to the declaration (idempotent)."""
+        for name, value in self._normalized_loader_fields().items():
+            setattr(self, name, value)

+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class DatasetRuntimeContext:
+    """Runtime inputs needed to turn a declarative dataset config into a Megatron Core config.
+
+    Training builds it with ``PretrainConfigContainer.dataset_runtime_context()``; standalone tools
+    build it with ``from_args()``. A value set here wins over the same field declared on the config;
+    ``None`` keeps the declared value (Megatron-Bridge recipes declare ``random_seed`` directly).
+    """
+
+    tokenizer: Any
+    random_seed: int | None = None
+    data_parallel_size: int | None = None
+    context_parallel_size: int | None = None
+    sequence_parallel_size: int | None = None
+    hybrid_context_parallel: bool | None = None
+    full_validation: bool | None = None
+    multiple_validation_sets: bool | None = None

+    def from_args(cls, args: Namespace, tokenizer: Any) -> "DatasetRuntimeContext":
+        """Context for tools that run from legacy arguments without a config container."""

+            tokenizer=tokenizer,
+            random_seed=getattr(args, "seed", None),
+            data_parallel_size=getattr(args, "data_parallel_size", None),
+            context_parallel_size=getattr(args, "context_parallel_size", None),
+            sequence_parallel_size=getattr(args, "tensor_model_parallel_size", 1)

+

+# infer. Applied last by ``DatasetArgumentGroupFactory`` (flag generation) and read by
+# ``gpt_dataset_config_from_args`` (args -> config) through the ``dest`` entries.
+LEGACY_ARG_MAP: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {
+    "path_to_cache": dict(arg_names=["--data-cache-path"], dest="data_cache_path", type=None),
+    "fast_cache_load": dict(
+        arg_names=["--dataloader-fast-cache-load"], dest="dataloader_fast_cache_load"
+    ),
+    "defer_npy_index_mmap": dict(
+        arg_names=["--dataloader-defer-npy-index-mmap"], dest="dataloader_defer_npy_index_mmap"
+    ),
+    "create_attention_mask": dict(
+        arg_names=["--no-create-attention-mask-in-dataloader"],
+        dest="create_attention_mask_in_dataloader",
+    ),
+    "inter_document_masking": dict(
+        arg_names=["--dataloader-inter-document-masking"], dest="dataloader_inter_document_masking"
+    ),
+    # These legacy flags register no argparse ``type`` (values stay the parsed strings).
+    "data_path": dict(nargs="*", type=None),
+    "train_data_path": dict(nargs="*", type=None),
+    "valid_data_path": dict(nargs="*", type=None),
+    "test_data_path": dict(nargs="*", type=None),
+    "per_dataset_sequences_path": dict(type=None),
+    # The parser leaves --dataset-type unset so that an explicit value is distinguishable from the
+    # dataclass default "gpt"; dataset_type_from_args maps None to "gpt" when no alias flag is set.
+    "dataset_type": dict(default=None),
+}
+
+# Legacy family flags kept as CLI aliases of dataset_type: flag -> (dest, dataset_type value).
+# The order is today's provider precedence (sft, then varlen, then fim).
+LEGACY_ALIAS_FLAGS: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {
+    "--sft": ("sft", "sft"),
+    "--use-varlen-dataset": ("use_varlen_dataset", "varlen"),
+    "--fim-data": ("fim_data", "fim"),
+}

+    "--sft": "Megatron SFT training. Alias of --dataset-type sft.",
+    "--use-varlen-dataset": (
+        "Train with VarlenDataset, a variable-length packed (THD) dataset that consumes "
+        "instruction-tuning data from a HuggingFace Hub repo id, a local parquet file, or a local "
+        "jsonl file. Schema (alpaca / sharegpt / openai-messages) is auto-detected from the dataset "
+        "columns. Mutually exclusive with --sft. Auto-picks a sequence packing scheduler when none "
+        "is given: dp_balanced. Combine with --mock-data for a synthetic lognormal sequence-length "
+        "distribution; see --varlen-mock-dataset-config-json. Alias of --dataset-type varlen."
+    ),
+    "--fim-data": "Whether to use the FIM dataset. Alias of --dataset-type fim.",
+}

+# knobs the legacy CLI never exposed (YAML / Python only).
+DATASET_CLI_EXCLUDE = [
+    "tokenizer",
+    "random_seed",
+    "data_parallel_size",
+    "context_parallel_size",
+    "sequence_parallel_size",
+    "hybrid_context_parallel",
+    "full_validation",
+    "multiple_validation_sets",
+    "sequence_length",
+    "blend",
+    "blend_per_split",
+    "sequences_per_dataset",
+    "fim_extra_tokens",
+    "drop_last_partial_validation_sequence",
+    "add_extra_token_to_sequence",
+    "pin_memory",
+    "persistent_workers",
+    "drop_last",
+]
+
+_CONTEXT_FIELDS = (
+    "random_seed",
+    "data_parallel_size",
+    "context_parallel_size",
+    "sequence_parallel_size",
+    "hybrid_context_parallel",
+    "full_validation",
+    "multiple_validation_sets",
+)
+_MCORE_RUNTIME_DEFAULTS = {
+    "data_parallel_size": 1,
+    "sequence_parallel_size": 0,
+    "hybrid_context_parallel": False,
+}
+_NOT_SERIALIZED = frozenset({"tokenizer", "sequence_length"})
+
+
+def dataset_type_from_args(args: Namespace, *, warn: bool = True) -> str:
+    """Resolve the dataset family from ``--dataset-type`` and the legacy alias flags.
+
+    The rule is stable under repetition, so ``validate_args`` (which writes the result back with
+    ``project_dataset_type_into_args``) and the config factories agree: an explicit ``dataset_type``
+    is consistent with alias flags when it equals their legacy resolution (``sft`` over ``varlen``
+    over ``fim``, as today's providers choose); any other disagreement is an error, a combination
+    that could not be written before. ``--sft`` with ``--use-varlen-dataset`` is rejected as
+    ``validate_args`` does. Several alias flags warn once (``warn=True``) where today the losers
+    are silently ignored.
+    """
+    explicit = getattr(args, "dataset_type", None)
+    aliases = [
+        family for _flag, (dest, family) in LEGACY_ALIAS_FLAGS.items() if getattr(args, dest, False)
+    ]
+    if "sft" in aliases and "varlen" in aliases:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "--use-varlen-dataset and --sft are mutually exclusive; both select the "
+            "packed-sequence dataset family. Pick one."
+        )
+    if explicit is not None and explicit not in DATASET_TYPES:
+        raise ValueError(f"--dataset-type must be one of {DATASET_TYPES}, got {explicit!r}.")
+    legacy = aliases[0] if aliases else None
+    if explicit is not None and legacy is not None and legacy != explicit:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"--dataset-type {explicit} contradicts the legacy flag(s) selecting {aliases}."
+        )
+    if warn and len(aliases) > 1:
+        _warn(f"{aliases} were all requested; '{aliases[0]}' wins, as in today's providers.")
+    if explicit is not None:
+        return explicit
+    return legacy or "gpt"
+
+
+def project_dataset_type_into_args(args: Namespace) -> str:
+    """Resolve the family once and write it back into ``args`` so unmigrated consumers follow it.
+
+    Called early in ``validate_args``, before the raw-flag checks and normalizations that read
+    ``args.sft`` / ``args.use_varlen_dataset`` / ``args.fim_data``: ``--dataset-type varlen`` then
+    auto-selects the packing scheduler, collates and batches exactly like ``--use-varlen-dataset``.
+    Flags the user passed are never cleared, so legacy namespaces are unchanged field by field, and
+    calling this again (or ``dataset_type_from_args``) returns the same family.
+    """
+    resolved = dataset_type_from_args(args)
+    args.dataset_type = resolved
+    for _flag, (dest, family) in LEGACY_ALIAS_FLAGS.items():
+        if family == resolved:
+            setattr(args, dest, True)
+    return resolved
+
+
+def _as_blend(blend: Any) -> tuple[list[str], list[float] | None] | None:
+    """YAML gives lists; Megatron Core expects a (prefixes, weights) tuple."""
+    if blend is None:
+        return None
+    prefixes, weights = blend
+    return (list(prefixes), None if weights is None else list(weights))
+
+
+@dataclass(kw_only=True)
+class GPTDatasetConfig(MCoreGPTDatasetConfig, DataloaderConfig):
